title: tune-nccl-streams-and-scheduling-to-improve-overlap-for-tensor-parallel
author: Aditi Rao
description:
Motivation: Tensor-parallel workloads on multi-GPU rigs often underutilize compute because NCCL collectives serialize on the default stream and block compute kernels. This PR introduces a conservative, opt-in scheduling and stream model that launches NCCL collectives on dedicated communication streams and schedules compute kernels on separate compute streams with explicit NVTX/events synchronization. The goal is to increase overlap of comm and compute for typical LLM inference patterns (KV cache reuse, long contexts, moderate batch sizes) without regressing stability or memory usage.

Summary of changes: added per-communicator comm streams, introduced runtime heuristics to decide overlap based on sequence length and batch size, converted key collective calls to use ncclGroupStart/ncclGroupEnd where useful, added event based sync points for KV cache slices, exposed env flags and runtime config to control aggressiveness, and added unit + multi-GPU perf tests.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in PR body (ENG-5127)
- [x] Implementation for comm streams and scheduler knobs
- [x] Backward-compatible: falls back to previous behavior when flag disabled
- [x] Multi-GPU perf test (8xA100) added to perf-canary job
- [x] CI green (build + unit + integration)

Design notes: For small sequence lengths (<128) overlap tends to harm latency due to extra stream syncs; we therefore only enable overlap when estimated comm time > threshold. We use a lightweight estimator derived from model hidden dim, tensor shape, and measured bandwidth. A runtime flag REDWOOD_TP_COMM_OVERLAP=auto|on|off controls behavior (default=auto). Comm streams are created per-NCCL-communicator group and reused to avoid stream churn. We also add a per-batch scheduling pass that identifies contiguous KV ranges and issues NCCL ops grouped to maximize group-size.

Stability and safety: Adds fallback to old-path if NCCL returns errors. Adds additional timeouts in the multi-gpu perf harness to detect hangs. Memory usage is unchanged for typical shapes; in corner cases we guard with a config to disable prefetching that could increase peak memory.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind REDWOOD_TP_COMM_OVERLAP and an operator-facing config in Dedicated/Private. Enable in canary for 10% traffic then 50% before global rollout.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps kernel-level changes minimal; primary optimizations are scheduling and NCCL usage patterns. Future work includes kernel fusion to further improve overlap benefits.

release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel performance via NCCL stream/scheduling optimizations. Reduced p90 latency and increased throughput for long-context workloads when overlap is enabled. Feature gated via REDWOOD_TP_COMM_OVERLAP (auto|on|off).
